tells: 1. The laugh doesn't build. From t=12.0 to 12.6 nobody's body changes; at 12.8 three people snap into poses all at once (green hoodie leans in, white-shirt woman lifts a hand to her chest, pink jacket turns his head). There's no breath intake, no shoulder rise and no rippling onset from person to person, so it reads as clip triggers (club-5-strip.png, all frames, centre front row)

2. Hands are glued flat on the tabletops in identical spread-finger 'piano' poses on four or five people at once, with no fidgeting, no drinks held and no weight shift, which is mannequin blocking (club-1-wide.png and club-6-held.png, front tables centre and right)

3. The face close is a game-NPC head: plastic orange skin with no pores or specular breakup, a stiff half-smile that doesn't reach the eyes or cheeks, dead brows, and pearls and collar edges with a hard dark outline from DOF fringing (club-4-face.png, whole face and collar)

4. The back of the house is flat black cardboard silhouettes, all standing at the same height, with no motion or rim light between strips, plus a sharp halo where front figures meet them (club-1-wide.png, middle band behind the front tables; club-2-mid.png, upper left)

5. Seating and contact: legs and chairs interpenetrate under the tables, the blonde woman in grey is seated with no visible chair support, bodies float with no contact shadow on the floor, and the far-right figures are cut off by darkness at the knees (club-1-wide.png, right of frame; club-2-mid.png, right table)

1. The wide is a class-photo lineup: three rows sit bolt upright facing camera with hands on knees in the same pose, and the back rows are a regular grid of identical standing-height figures, some visibly standing in the aisles with arms hanging (theatre-1-wide.png and theatre-6-held.png, whole frame; left edge figures standing with hands out)

2. The laugh is an instant open-mouth switch on a still body: in the strip, mouths open between 12.6 and 12.8 while torsos, heads and hands barely move. No one tips back, rocks or claps, and the guy in the cap freezes his hands mid-gesture (theatre-5-strip.png, front row, frames 4-6)

3. The face close has a slack, gaping mouth with a black void inside and no teeth shape or tongue, glassy unfocused eyes looking down, and wax skin with no cheek raise or eye crinkle, so this is not a laugh face (theatre-4-face.png, mouth and eyes)

4. Contact: seated people float in front of the red seats instead of sinking into them, shins and feet dissolve into black, there's no armrest contact, and a man is half-cut through the seat back (theatre-2-mid.png, front row lower half; theatre-3-mid.png, right edge man in cap)

5. Lighting is flat frontal and the same on every face across depth, with dark outlines ringing every figure (a DOF/outline halo) and back rows that read as cutout cards, not volume; the bright spot cans burn with no flare or haze interaction (theatre-2-mid.png, back rows; theatre-1-wide.png, top lights)

1. Everyone in the front row has the same posture: shoulders forward, arms straight down, hands planted on the thighs, which is a T-pose-derived rest, not how people sit for a comic. There's no crossed legs, no leaning on a neighbour and no drink (openmic-1-wide.png and openmic-6-held.png, front row; openmic-3-mid.png, all hands)

2. In the laugh, only faces change: the mouths of the green-top girl and the bob-haired girl open at 12.6 to 12.8 and heads turn toward each other in a canned 'share the joke' beat, while the rest of the row is static or only drifts its gaze. Nobody's chest heaves or shoulders bounce (openmic-5-strip.png, centre pair, frames 4-6)

3. Open mouths are dark slots with tiny tooth strips, and the bob-haired girl's eyelashes and fringe render as jagged black spikes; the eyes have no wet specular and no lid tension (openmic-2-mid.png, right-centre girl's face; openmic-3-mid.png, same girl)

4. Hair is helmet-like everywhere. The face close's hair is a solid mass with a stippled, aliased fringe at the ear and no flyaways, and the background blonde has a sharp cutout edge (openmic-4-face.png, hair behind ear and right background)

5. Contact and space: the front row floats in a black void without a visible floor or chair under several people, the knees of the pink-legged girl are lit hotter than her face, the back rows are again uniform-height silhouettes, and the room behind is an empty shoebox with a lone door card (openmic-1-wide.png, lower third and left wall door)
